questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code keeps the permission cache consistent with role changes? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A user is a member of a group, and an administrator changes that group's roles through update_group_roles. When do the group members' cached permission sets stop reflecting the old roles?
choices: Only when each member's 15 minute entry expires, because the group change does not touch the cache
After the transaction commits, when expire_many deletes the entries of all members that were read in the transaction
Immediately inside the transaction, because assigning role_ids triggers a cache delete on every membership
Never until the next deploy, because the cache key includes the VERSION constant

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of race_condition_ttl: 10.seconds in PermissionCache.fetch?
choices: It makes every entry expire 10 seconds earlier than TTL to leave a safety margin
It rejects reads of entries older than 10 seconds when the database is reachable
When an entry has just expired, one caller recomputes it while others briefly keep receiving the stale value, which avoids many callers rebuilding the permission set at once
It delays cache writes by 10 seconds so that in-flight transactions can finish first

questions.prompt: Authorizer#allowed? is called on every authenticated request. If the cache store becomes unreachable and Rails.cache.fetch raises, what happens to the request?
choices: The exception propagates out of allowed? and require!, and nothing in this code rescues it, so the request fails with a server error
The request is denied with 403 Forbidden because the Denied error is raised
The block runs anyway, so permissions are rebuilt from the database and the request proceeds
The permission set is treated as empty and allowed? returns false
